findings.explanation: The same field and app field name the Splunk Add-on for RabbitMQ, REST API Modular Input (1546) and Universal Forwarder monitor inputs as the collectors; the Unix and Linux add-on (833 in the cached catalog) does not collect RabbitMQ management or broker logs, so the appended sentence and app suffix contradict the rest of the text.
findings.quote: Collected via Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux (Splunkbase 833) modular input or scripted poll into the index named in the SPL.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the Unix and Linux add-on attribution from dataSources and app (or state precisely what it is used for, for example host OS metrics).

findings.explanation: The primary collector is not identified (no name, ID or sourcetype source) and the sourcetypes `rabbitmq:management:api:json`, `rabbitmq:server` and `rabbitmq:sasl` are asserted without grounding; it is unclear that any such add-on exists or emits these names.
findings.quote: **Splunk Add-on for RabbitMQ** (search Splunkbase for the current listing; after install, open `$SPLUNK_HOME/etc/apps/<the_app>/default/inputs.conf` and copy the real modular-input stanza names
findings.suggested_fix: Name the add-on and Splunkbase ID if one exists and list the sourcetypes it really emits; otherwise document the REST API Modular Input (1546) and UF monitor setup with the sourcetypes you define.

findings.explanation: Current RabbitMQ releases (3.7+) merged SASL output into the main log, and HiPE was removed from Erlang/OTP 24, while the UC targets Rabbit 3.x/4.x. Also the main stanza `monitor:///var/log/rabbitmq/*.log` would already match any -sasl.log file under the rabbitmq:server sourcetype.
findings.suggested_fix: Check the logging documentation for your RabbitMQ version; drop the SASL/HiPE feed if it no longer exists, or exclude it from the main glob if it does.

findings.explanation: Marked verified with reviewer 'uplift-handcraft-2026-04', an automated author; the add-on, sourcetypes and log paths above are unconfirmed and no SME sign-off is recorded.
findings.suggested_fix: Downgrade status until an SME has reviewed it against a lab OpenStack/RabbitMQ deployment.

findings.explanation: The SPL assigns critical/warning/watch severities with different rules (memory or disk alarm, not running, partition and OOM are critical; churn thresholds 6, 25 and 40 are unmentioned); the description flattens them into one list, calls `_time` a metric, and ends with a title-word list with a trailing comma.
findings.quote: Threshold bundle: `mready` > 2000, `oom_n` > 0, `memdisk_n` >= 3, or `n_part_l` >= 1; aggregation grain: `host`; metrics: `_time`, `mem_alarm_f`, `disk_alarm_f`. Watch terms: OpenStack, Control, Plane, RabbitMQ, Alarms,.
findings.suggested_fix: Describe the severity ladder: critical (memory/disk alarm, node not running, partition, OOM), warning (3+ resource-limit log lines, partition text, deep Oslo queues, churn bursts), watch (low-level signals).

findings.explanation: dataSources lists five feeds (management API, server log, SASL, syslog, optional journald). The implementation text also stops mid-sentence ('...Ansible work windows') with no final punctuation.
findings.suggested_fix: State the actual number of feeds and finish the sentence.

findings.explanation: The RabbitMQ alarms page covers memory and free disk space alarms; file descriptor exhaustion is a separate limit, not an alarm, so the title overstates the page.
findings.suggested_fix: Retitle as 'RabbitMQ — Alarms (memory and free disk space)' and add the file descriptors page separately if needed.

findings.explanation: Closing note is promotional and unverifiable and refers to UC-19.1.46 and UC-19.1.26 (a Nutanix UC) as instruction sources, which makes the document depend on unrelated sibling content.
findings.quote: That structural mirror is what makes a greenfield private cloud SRE team productive in a single day of pairing with this document
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the closing note and the cross-references to UC-19.1.26/19.1.46 for setup instructions.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: This OpenStack RabbitMQ control-plane use case sits in subcategory 19.1 (Cisco UCS), whose grounding guide covers UCS, Intersight, HyperFlex, Nutanix and similar HCI platforms and has no OpenStack content; it appears misfiled.

REST-polled API events carry the poller's host, not the Rabbit node, so API-derived alarms (`stats ... by host`) will not line up with log-derived rows keyed on the broker host unless host is overridden; `coalesce(mem_alarm, memAlarm, mem_alarm, ...)` repeats an argument; the partition test `part_txt!=" null"` has a stray leading space.

summary: An extensive RabbitMQ health design, but it is filed under Cisco UCS, mixes in boilerplate that credits the Unix/Linux add-on, depends on an add-on and sourcetypes that are never pinned down, uses legacy SASL/HiPE log assumptions, and is marked verified by an agent reviewer.
